claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53 produced by traditional melting routes.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Under dynamic adiabatic deformation, conventional HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformation, and rapid failure.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering or hot isostatic pressing can incorporate nanoscale HfO2 dispersoids into HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed processing route will produce a uniform nanoscale HfO2 second-phase dispersion in the alloy matrix.
Nanoscale HfO2 particles will act as dislocation-pinning obstacles during high-rate deformation.
Dislocation obstruction by the HfO2 dispersoids will increase dynamic strain hardening.
The dispersoid-mediated increase in strain hardening will delay the onset of localized shear bands.
Delayed shear localization will promote more uniform deformation.
Delayed catastrophic localization will reduce the rate of impact-induced energy release.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have greater dynamic yield strength than the conventional baseline.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have greater strain hardening than the conventional baseline.
The intervention will increase fracture strain by several percent relative to the baseline.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will show greater resistance to dynamic localization than the baseline.
The predicted effects apply around a strain rate of 10^3 s^-1 at room temperature in an inert environment under conditions with significant adiabatic heating.
